To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the use of text mining techniques in the banking environment is not a new idea but the use of text in the context of structured customer and account profiles is a new idea, (2) this idea can be implemented by using the data mining algorithms that we have used in LIPTUS, (3) the implementation of this idea is technically challenging but not impossible, (4) the value of this idea can be demonstrated in the banking environment through specific customer intelligence application,

(a) LIPTUS can associate customer interactions with the customer and account profile information in an existing data-warehouse, (b) this association enables analytics spanning the structured and unstructured data, and (c) the analytics derived can be used to improve the customer service experience and to increase the customer's lifetime value.

1. LIPTUS associates structured and unstructured data, 2. LIPTUS discovers new associations between structured and unstructured customer information, 3. LIPTUS enables analytics spanning customer profiles, account information, and customer interactions, 4. LIPTUS can be deployed in any banking environment

the following: (1) how to extract structured and unstructured data from the interaction (phone calls and emails), (2) how to associate the extracted information with the customer and account profile, and (3) how to analyze the association to derive actionable insights.
the following question: how can a bank use its customer interactions to improve its understanding of customers?
the development of a scalable and robust tool for associating structured and semi-structured data.
